script.problem: It uses a dash. No em dashes or en dashes.

terra.problem: Saying Israel was about to lie down under every green tree adds a sequence the text does not give.
The punchline makes light of the prostitution imagery used to describe Israel’s serious sin.
Saying they spoke while the chains were still hitting the ground adds a specific moment not given in the text.
The verse presents washing with lye and soap as a hypothetical, not as something Israel actually did.
Calling the LORD’s picture a joke makes the scriptural image itself the joke.
The verse says those seeking her will find her in mating season; it does not say they know exactly where she will be.
The allowance joke introduces a modern parent scenario and makes Israel’s idolatry the target of the joke.
Israel calls on the LORD for help, not on the gods they made. The LORD challenges those gods to save Israel, not themselves.
The cooling-cookie joke makes a comparison that puts Israel down for forgetting the LORD.
Days without number does not establish that forty days would be a short stretch by comparison.
Calling Assyria a mighty empire adds a fact outside the passage without a supporting reference.
The passage says Egypt will disappoint Israel; it does not say nobody gets saved there.
The passage does not say Egypt wins nothing for Israel; it says Israel will be disappointed by Egypt.
Saying no army is coming adds a categorical claim the passage does not make.
Even a thief manages that much is a put-down rather than a respectful explanation of the comparison.
The verse describes a brazen look and refusal to be ashamed; it does not establish as fact that they feel no shame at all.
Saying they had no shame states their feelings as fact. The verse says they refused to be ashamed.
